newsitem.title: USA: Airport Systems sees Q3 loss, Q4 recovery.
newsitem.headline: Airport Systems sees Q3 loss, Q4 recovery.

text.p: Airport Systems International Inc said Friday the timing of some shipments had hurt its sales for the third fiscal quarter ending January 31 and would result in a loss for the quarter.

"Based on our current schedules, however, we fully expect to make up this shortfall in the fourth fiscal quarter and to be solidly in the black for fiscal 1997 as a whole," said Keith Cowan, president and chief executive officer.
Airport Systems makes equipment and airfield signs to aid the in-flight navigation and ground movement of aircraft.
In the year-ago third quarter the company reported sales of $3.7 million and a net loss of $74,000, or $0.03 per share.

Airport Systems said it had received several contracts totalling about $3 million. The contracts involve the company's shipment and installation of equipment at various sites in North America, Europe, the Pacific Rim and the Middle East.

"Although these contracts extend the positive trend in our business that emerged in the first fiscal half, the timing of shipments has adversely affected sales in the three months ending January 31, 1997, that will result in a loss for the quarter," Cowan said in a statement.
Airport Systems shares were trading up 1/4 to six.
